hero.name: Fay Lyu (HazezZ)
hero.subtitle: Optimization · Formal Methods · Game Theory · Data
hero.positioning: I’m an undergraduate math student working on optimization theory and formal verification. Right now I’m (1) building a reusable Isabelle/HOL development for submodular greedy guarantees, and (2) studying when duality/lower-bound formulations become trivial under invariances (and how to “fix the gauge” to recover information). This page is a 30-second research entry with links to notes and repos.

interests.title: Research interests (current)
items: Optimization theory (especially algorithmic structure and first-order methods)
Game theory (especially as a mathematical modeling language for strategic structure)
Formal methods for mathematics (Isabelle/HOL, proof structure, reusability)
I care about explicit assumptions, reusable abstractions, and verifiable reasoning

projects_section.title: Current Projects (3 entry points)
projects_section.lead: Editorial summary cards: problem, method, contribution, status, and links. Longer technical context lives in the notes.

projects.title: An Ongoing Isabelle Research Project: Formalising Submodular Greedy
projects.problem: Formalize the classical greedy (1−1/e) approximation guarantee for monotone submodular maximization under a cardinality constraint.
projects.method: Split the development into constructive and approximation-analysis layers, then encode assumptions and intermediate lemmas explicitly in Isabelle/HOL.
projects.contribution: Reusable formal scaffolding + proof decomposition notes for a machine-checkable development path.

projects.title: Spring 2026 | A New Research Direction (Cornell ORIE)
projects.problem: Identify a nontrivial dual / lower-bound framework for a graph-relative-difference distance-fitting objective (B-encoded).
projects.method: Compare DC/Fenchel dualization with plain Lagrangian duals and diagnose degeneracy from unconstrainedness + translation invariance.
projects.status: Active · DC/Fenchel route is informative; next step is tighter relaxations (gauge-fixing / augmented Lagrangian / ADMM).
projects.contribution: Dual-framework comparison, structural diagnosis of trivial bounds, and note-driven refinement of the problem formulation.
projects.status_detail: DC/Fenchel route is informative; next step is tighter relaxations (gauge-fixing / augmented Lagrangian / ADMM).
projects.status_display: Active · DC/Fenchel route is informative; next step is tighter relaxations (gauge-fixing / augmented Lagrangian / ADMM).

projects.title: Metalcore Piano Lab | From Audio to Chart (WIP)
projects.problem: Map continuous audio (or MIDI) into a playable rhythm-game chart as a structured discretization problem.
projects.method: Onset/beat detection, tempo tracking, segmentation, alignment, and playability-oriented constraints.
projects.status: Active · Browser prototype works end-to-end; chart quality and scaling heuristics are being refined.
projects.contribution: Browser-native prototype + reproducible notes on assumptions, failure modes, and optimization targets.

now_section.title: What I’m Currently Thinking About
now_section.lead: Questions and themes I’m actively using to steer reading, proof work, and modeling choices.

now_items: Which dual formulations remain informative under non-identifiability / translation invariance, and which collapse to trivial lower bounds.
How to design reusable proof structure in Isabelle/HOL so formalization artifacts scale beyond one theorem statement.
When a “natural” relaxation is too loose: what structural fix (gauge-fixing, constraints, augmentation) restores useful information.
How signal-like inputs (audio, temporal traces) can be mapped into discrete, computable structures without losing interpretability.
How optimization / formal methods / modeling can share one language of explicit assumptions and reproducible abstractions.
